archetypes.name: cap-hit-sidecar-path
archetypes.rationale: The plan makes a precise but internally ambiguous claim about where launch-review.sh writes the cap-hit sidecar (describing it as both '${OUTPUT}.cap-hit' and 'i.e. ${OUTPUT}.raw.cap-hit when output is ${OUTPUT}.raw'), and the correctness of tier_raw_is_scout_json and the pre-tier rm -f hinge on which description is accurate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/launch-review.sh and locate where the cap-hit sidecar file path is constructed and written, noting the exact relationship between the --output argument and the sidecar basename. Cross-check this against the plan's UPDATED scout-dynamic-archetypes.sh section, which simultaneously states 'sidecar is ${OUTPUT}.cap-hit per launch-review.sh line 186' and 'i.e. ${OUTPUT}.raw.cap-hit when output is ${OUTPUT}.raw' — determine whether these are consistent or contradictory, and which path tier_raw_is_scout_json must actually probe. Verify that the pre-tier 'rm -f ${tier_raw}.cap-hit' clears the correct path given the actual naming convention, and that a stale Codex sidecar cannot survive into a Claude tier invocation due to a probe-path mismatch. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: print-mode-tool-exec
archetypes.rationale: The plan's entire --read-tools approach rests on the assertion that 'claude --print' supports --add-dir/--allowedTools tool execution; if --print silently ignores tool scaffolding or returns zero-length output on Read calls, the scout produces zero archetypes with no error signal and no harness regression.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/launch-claude-subprocess.sh to understand the current --print invocation and how --read-tools would change it, then check scripts/test-launch-claude-subprocess.sh to determine whether any assertion actually validates that Read tool calls execute and return content rather than just checking that the correct argv is constructed. Look for whether the plan provides a real verification step beyond the 'verify at impl time' note, and whether the harness can distinguish a correctly-formed argv from a launch that silently produces empty output because --print does not feed tool results back to the model in this invocation shape. Check whether any fallback or SCOUT_STATUS signal is produced when --read-tools mode returns empty raw. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: design-presence-env
archetypes.rationale: The plan threads --codex-present/$CODEX_PRESENT into plan-review-loop.sh and scout-plan-archetypes-wrapper.sh but does not identify where the design flow initialises CODEX_PRESENT, so an unset variable silently locks the plan-review scout into single-tier Claude-only mode even when Codex is available.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/design/scripts/plan-review-loop.sh and skills/design/scripts/scout-plan-archetypes-wrapper.sh to find where CODEX_PRESENT and CURSOR_PRESENT are expected to come from, then read the design session setup path (e.g. scripts/session-setup.sh, scripts/write-design-current-env.sh, or equivalent bootstrap scripts) to determine whether presence-detection logic that sets these variables exists for the design flow. Compare against the implement path (scripts/write-session-env.sh or implement-bootstrap.sh) to verify whether the design flow has equivalent plumbing or whether the plan's forwarding changes will silently pass empty strings and leave the scout in single-tier mode despite Codex being available. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
